intro: Optometrists combine clinical judgment, patient care and precise equipment, so their matches are in health science, teaching and research. The closest of the 25 careers below is Medical Dosimetrists, with a 70% skill match and a BLS May 2025 median of $147,470, which is 8% more than the $136,570 optometrists earn.
why_it_works: An exam day means testing vision, reading results and explaining options to patients of every age. O*NET rates social perceptiveness at 3.88 out of 5 for this job, and coordination, judgment and problem solving at 3.38. Dosimetry, teaching and clinical research use the same precision. Because your pay is already high, only 2 matches pay more. The gaps are instructing and analyzing operations.
tips: Teaching in an optometry program is a way to step back from clinic hours while using your expertise.
Natural Sciences Managers earn $167,220, which is 22% more, if you move into research leadership.
Industry roles in eyewear and device companies are not separate careers in this data, but many hire optometrists.

faq.q: What jobs can former optometrists do?
faq.a: The closest matches are Medical Dosimetrists (70%), postsecondary health specialties teachers (67%) and clinical research coordinators (67%), based on O*NET 31.0. Genetic Counselors are 64% matched and earn $100,040, which is 27% less than the $136,570 optometrist median.

faq.q: Which careers for optometrists pay more?
faq.a: Only 2 of the 25 matches pay more. Natural Sciences Managers earn $167,220 (22% more) and Medical Dosimetrists $147,470 (8% more), according to BLS May 2025 data. Clinical research coordinators earn $167,220 for their broader BLS group, close to research management.

faq.q: Do optometrists need another degree to change careers?
faq.a: No. All 25 matches need no more education than optometrists already have, including all of the top 10. A bachelor's or master's degree is common in close matches, so your doctor of optometry degree more than covers formal requirements for every role on this list.

The skills that most often need work are operations analysis, complex problem solving, equipment selection and instructing. Judgment already rates 3.38 out of 5 for optometrists in O*NET, so teaching and research methods are the main steps outside the exam room.
